excerpt: Implement a non-compliance reporting policy for our Responsible Scaling Commitments as part of reaching ASL-3. The policy should allow for anonymous feedback, with an appropriate reporting chain.
paraphrase: A non-compliance reporting policy allowing anonymous feedback with an appropriate reporting chain must be implemented upon reaching ASL-3.

excerpt: Ensuring that we never train a model that passes an ASL evaluation threshold is a difficult task. Models are trained in discrete sizes, they require effort to evaluate mid-training, and serious, meaningful evaluations may be very time consuming, since they will likely require fine-tuning.
paraphrase: Preventing training a model past an ASL threshold is difficult due to discrete training sizes and the time-consuming nature of meaningful evaluations requiring fine-tuning.

excerpt: This means there is a risk of overshooting an ASL threshold when we intended to stop short of it.
paraphrase: There is thus a risk of overshooting the intended ASL threshold.

excerpt: We mitigate this risk by creating a buffer: we have intentionally designed our ASL evaluations to trigger at slightly lower capability levels than those we are concerned about, while ensuring we evaluate at defined, regular intervals (specifically every 4x increase in effective compute, as defined below) in order to limit the amount of overshoot that is possible.
paraphrase: This overshoot risk is mitigated by a buffer: evaluations trigger below actual concern levels and occur at regular intervals of every 4x increase in effective compute.

excerpt: We have aimed to set the size of our safety buffer to 6x (larger than our 4x evaluation interval) so model training can continue safely while evaluations take place.
paraphrase: The safety buffer is aimed at 6x, larger than the 4x evaluation interval, to allow safe continued training during evaluation.

excerpt: Correct execution of this scheme will result in us training models that just barely pass the test for ASL-N, are still slightly below our actual threshold of concern (due to our buffer), and then pausing training and deployment of that model unless the corresponding safety measures are ready.
paraphrase: If executed correctly, models will just barely pass the ASL-N test while remaining below the true concern threshold, with training and deployment paused unless safety measures are ready.

excerpt: Model evaluations: Evaluations are tests that are designed to detect dangerous capabilities. They should be conservative "warning signs" so as to avoid accidentally overshooting a critical safety threshold.
paraphrase: Evaluations are tests to detect dangerous capabilities and should be conservative warning signs to avoid overshooting critical thresholds.

context_stem: Model evaluations: Evaluations are tests that are designed to detect dangerous capabilities...
excerpt: Progressive difficulty: Evaluations may also consist of multiple difficulty stages, such that later stages are only run if earlier evaluations show warning signs (e.g. we might run a simple multiple choice eval for certain risks, avoiding a more thorough evaluation unless the model achieves high performance on this simpler eval).
paraphrase: Evaluations may have progressive difficulty stages, running more thorough tests only after earlier simpler evaluations show warning signs.

context_stem: Model evaluations: Evaluations are tests that are designed to detect dangerous capabilities...
excerpt: Previous evaluations: We previously carried out similar evaluations on a model similar to Claude 2 for capabilities related to biological risks and collaborated with the Alignment Research Center to evaluate autonomous capabilities. Both evaluations showed the model as strictly below ASL-3.
paraphrase: Similar prior evaluations of a Claude 2-like model for biological risk and autonomous capability (with ARC) showed results strictly below ASL-3.

excerpt: Timing: During model training and fine-tuning, Anthropic will conduct an evaluation of its models for next-ASL capabilities both (1) after every 4x jump in effective compute, including if this occurs mid-training, and (2) every 3 months to monitor fine-tuning/tooling/etc improvements.
paraphrase: Anthropic will evaluate models for next-ASL capabilities after every 4x jump in effective compute and every 3 months to monitor fine-tuning improvements.
stated_bar: every 4x jump in effective compute; every 3 months

context_stem: Timing: During model training and fine-tuning, Anthropic will conduct an evaluation...
excerpt: Effective Compute: We define effective compute as roughly the amount of compute it would have taken to train a model if no improvements to pretraining or fine-tuning techniques are included. This is operationalized by tracking the scaling of model capabilities (e.g. cross-entropy loss on a test set).
paraphrase: Effective compute is defined as the compute needed absent pretraining/fine-tuning improvements, operationalized via tracking model capability scaling such as cross-entropy loss.

excerpt: Investment in evaluations: An inherent difficulty of an evaluations regime is that it is not currently possible to truly upper-bound the capabilities of generative models.
paraphrase: A core challenge of the evaluations regime is the impossibility of truly upper-bounding generative model capabilities.

context_stem: Investment in evaluations: An inherent difficulty of an evaluations regime...
excerpt: However, it is important that we are evaluating models with close to our best capabilities elicitation techniques, to avoid underestimating the capabilities it would be possible for a malicious actor to elicit if the model were stolen.
paraphrase: Evaluations must use near-best elicitation techniques to avoid underestimating what a malicious actor could elicit from a stolen model.

context_stem: Investment in evaluations: An inherent difficulty of an evaluations regime...
excerpt: False negatives due to harmlessness: While there are commercial and research incentives to develop maximally effective post-training techniques, certain evaluations may result in false negatives when used on commercial models.
paraphrase: Despite incentives for effective post-training, evaluations run on commercial models may produce false negatives.

context_stem: Investment in evaluations: An inherent difficulty of an evaluations regime...
excerpt: For example, harmlessness techniques may cause the model to refuse to assist with dangerous activities even when the underlying capability is present. Proper effort must be invested to avoid this type of false negative.
paraphrase: Harmlessness training may cause refusals masking present dangerous capability, so effort must be invested to avoid such false negatives.
